title: Track a small project
description: Track a small project with a next action, a waiting item, and a done item.
oneStarDescription: Write three columns or a list with at least one next action.
twoStarDescription: When something changes, move it and write the date.
threeStarDescription: For an item that is waiting, write who it is waiting on, and send or make the request.

title: Trim a short video
description: Cut a clip so it starts and ends on the action, and leave the unused ends out.
oneStarDescription: Set a start and an end so the waiting at both ends is gone.
twoStarDescription: Play the trim and show that the action you cared about is still there.
threeStarDescription: Save the trimmed copy without deleting the original, and say which is which.

title: Tune a string to a reference
description: Tune one string of an instrument to a reference note, and say when it is close.
oneStarDescription: Play a reference note and the string, and say whether the string is lower or higher.
twoStarDescription: Turn the tuner the right way and stop when a tuner or a listener says it matches.
threeStarDescription: Compare that string with the next string by the method your instrument uses, and say whether the pair agrees.

title: Turn on a second sign-in check
description: Add a second check to an account and show that sign-in now asks for it.
oneStarDescription: Find the second-check setting on an account you control.
twoStarDescription: Turn it on by the service's own steps and sign out.
threeStarDescription: Sign in again and show that the service asks for the second check, or show the confirmation screen.

title: Find a book in a library catalog
description: Find a known book in a library catalog and then on the shelf or in the request system.
oneStarDescription: Search by title or author and open the record that matches the book you want.
twoStarDescription: Read the branch and the shelf mark, or the request button if it is not on the shelf.
threeStarDescription: Find it on the shelf or place a request, and say which you did.

title: Turn leftovers into another meal
description: Use leftover food in a second meal while it still looks and smells as it did when you stored it.
oneStarDescription: Point to one stored food and say what meal it can become.
twoStarDescription: Make that meal and show the leftover in the new dish.
threeStarDescription: Set aside one stored item you will not use, and say the visible reason, such as a change in smell or look.

title: Wash clothes by the label
description: Read a care label and wash a load that matches it.
oneStarDescription: Point to the wash temperature or cycle symbol on a garment and say what you will do.
twoStarDescription: Put together only clothes whose labels allow the same wash, and leave one item out on purpose.
threeStarDescription: After the wash, show one result, such as a dye bleed or a still-dirty mark, and say what you would change next time.

title: Water a plant by checking the soil
description: Decide whether to water a plant by feeling the soil, not by the calendar alone.
oneStarDescription: Touch the soil below the surface and say whether it is dry or damp.
twoStarDescription: Water only if it is dry, or leave it and say why.
threeStarDescription: Look the next day and say whether the plant or the soil suggests you gave too much or too little.

title: Welcome a new person
description: Help a new person take a first useful step in a group you already know.
oneStarDescription: Greet the person, say your name, and show them where to start.
twoStarDescription: Tell them one norm that would embarrass them if they learned it late.
threeStarDescription: Introduce them to one person relevant to why they came, and step back.

title: Work one focus block
description: Work on one task for a block you chose, and record what pulled you away.
oneStarDescription: Write the task and the end time before you start.
twoStarDescription: Work until the end time, and write down each interruption instead of following it.
threeStarDescription: From the list of interruptions, change one thing in the room or the device before the next block.

title: Work out a time-zone gap
description: Convert a time in one place to the local time in another, and check it.
oneStarDescription: Write the two places and the local time you are converting.
twoStarDescription: Convert the time with a source you can show, including the date if it changes.
threeStarDescription: Propose a meeting time that is inside waking hours in both places, and show both local times.

title: Wrap a parcel so it stays closed
description: Wrap an object so the paper stays closed when you pick it up.
oneStarDescription: Cut paper that covers the object with overlap, and fold the first seam.
twoStarDescription: Fold both ends so no open flap hangs out.
threeStarDescription: Pick the parcel up by the top and secure any flap that opens.

title: Write a caption that matches
description: Write a caption that says what a picture shows and what it does not.
oneStarDescription: Write one sentence that a viewer could check against the picture.
twoStarDescription: Add a second sentence of context you actually know, and mark it as context.
threeStarDescription: Delete one claim you cannot see or source, and leave the caption without it.

title: Write a group update
description: Tell a group what changed, what you need, and what you are not asking.
oneStarDescription: Write three sentences: what changed, what happens next, and who it is for.
twoStarDescription: Add one request with a time, or say that you need nothing.
threeStarDescription: Remove a sentence that does not help the reader act or understand.

title: Write a handover note
description: Leave a note so another person can continue a task without asking you the basics.
oneStarDescription: Write what is done and what is not.
twoStarDescription: Write the next action and where the files or objects are.
threeStarDescription: Write one thing that will go wrong if the next person does not know it.

title: Write a journal entry
description: Write an entry that records what happened and one thing you noticed.
oneStarDescription: Write what happened, where, and when, in a few sentences.
twoStarDescription: Add one sensory detail or one thought you had at the time, and mark which it is.
threeStarDescription: End with a question you still have, rather than a moral.

title: Write a packing list for someone else
description: Write a packing list another person can use for a trip you both understand.
oneStarDescription: Ask the destination, the length, and one activity before you write the list.
twoStarDescription: Write items a person could pack, grouped, without brand names they do not need.
threeStarDescription: Hear one item they refuse, take it off or say why you would keep it, and agree the list.

title: Write a recipe card someone can cook
description: Write a recipe from a dish you made so another person could cook it.
oneStarDescription: Write the ingredients you used and the steps in order.
twoStarDescription: Add one check the cook can taste or see, such as 'until the onion is soft'.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone to read it and add the step they say is missing.

title: Write a review with evidence
description: Review a book, place, or tool by tying each judgement to something you can point to.
oneStarDescription: Write who the thing is for and one judgement.
twoStarDescription: Under the judgement, cite a scene, a feature, or a quote you can find again.
threeStarDescription: Name one kind of reader or user for whom your judgement may not hold.

title: Write a short scene
description: Write a scene in which a character wants something and the situation changes.
oneStarDescription: Write a scene that shows what a character wants.
twoStarDescription: Add a turn so the character does not end where they started.
threeStarDescription: Remove one sentence that explains the feeling instead of showing it, and say what the scene still shows.

title: Write a specific thank-you
description: Thank someone for a particular thing they did, not only for being kind.
oneStarDescription: Write a note that names what the person did.
twoStarDescription: Add what that act made possible for you.
threeStarDescription: Send or give the note, and leave out one vague praise you were tempted to add.

title: Write a spreadsheet formula
description: Write a formula that answers a question, and check it against a hand calculation.
oneStarDescription: Write a formula that adds or averages cells you can point to.
twoStarDescription: Calculate the same result by hand or with a calculator and show that it matches.
threeStarDescription: Change one input and say whether the result moved as you expected.

title: Write steps someone can follow
description: Write steps for a task you can do, and watch another person try them.
oneStarDescription: Write the steps of a small task in order, starting from what the person has in front of them.
twoStarDescription: Let someone else follow the steps without your extra talk, and note where they stop.
threeStarDescription: Rewrite the step that stopped them and show that the new line answers the stop.

title: Active listening
description: Understand another person’s point before responding by giving attention, asking clarifying questions and checking your interpretation.
oneStarDescription: In a short conversation, let the other person finish and restate their main point in your own words.
twoStarDescription: Ask at least two relevant follow-up questions and confirm whether your summary is accurate.
threeStarDescription: Summarise the different concerns in a longer conversation and distinguish what was said from your interpretation.

title: Inspect astronomical images systematically
description: Describe visible features in a telescope image and record its context and limitations without claiming scientific conclusions that the image alone cannot support.
oneStarDescription: Record the visible object or feature and distinguish description from an inference about its cause.
twoStarDescription: Compare two images using their available context and identify visible similarities or differences without assuming the capture conditions are identical.
threeStarDescription: Prepare a note listing the image context, observed features, uncertainty and the additional data needed to test an interpretation.

title: Build a reasoned written argument
description: State a clear claim, support it with relevant reasons or evidence, and address objections without confusing assertion with proof.
oneStarDescription: Write a thesis or central claim that can be understood and discussed, rather than a broad topic label.
twoStarDescription: Write a short argument with at least two relevant reasons or pieces of evidence and explain how they support the claim.
threeStarDescription: Revise the argument to acknowledge a plausible counterpoint and explain why the claim still holds or needs narrowing.

title: Write clear, coherent paragraphs
description: Develop paragraphs around a central idea, using relevant supporting material and transitions that help a reader follow the reasoning.
oneStarDescription: Write a paragraph in which each sentence supports one identifiable main idea.
twoStarDescription: Support the main point with relevant explanation, evidence or an example and connect sentences clearly.
threeStarDescription: Revise a multi-paragraph piece so each paragraph has a clear role and transitions connect the sequence.

title: Use a compass and orient a map
description: Orient a map to the surrounding terrain and use a compass to determine a direction or bearing on a suitable practice route.
oneStarDescription: Use visible landmarks and a compass to align a map with the surrounding direction.
twoStarDescription: Identify a direction between two mapped points and follow it on a clear, low-risk practice route.
threeStarDescription: Explain when declination matters for the map and region and check the direction against visible terrain features.

title: Write concisely
description: Make writing direct and readable by removing repetition, vague phrasing and words that do not contribute to the intended meaning.
oneStarDescription: Revise a short paragraph by deleting repetition while preserving its meaning.
twoStarDescription: Rewrite a wordy passage with more specific verbs and nouns, then check that no key detail was lost.
threeStarDescription: Produce a concise version for a specific reader and explain which details were kept, moved or removed.

title: Constructive conflict resolution
description: Clarify disagreements by listening to the people involved, identifying the disputed issue and agreeing on a practical next step when possible.
oneStarDescription: Describe the disagreement in neutral language and state each side’s concern without assigning blame.
twoStarDescription: Ask each party what outcome matters and suggest at least two possible next steps.
threeStarDescription: Record a mutually accepted action, who will do it and when to revisit whether it worked.

title: Give and use constructive writing feedback
description: Review another person’s writing against its purpose, describe specific issues respectfully, and turn feedback into an actionable revision plan.
oneStarDescription: Give feedback on one clear strength and one concrete improvement, referring to the relevant passage.
twoStarDescription: Separate structure and argument issues from sentence-level corrections and explain which change matters most.
threeStarDescription: Create a list of changes, decide which suggestions to apply and explain why some feedback may not fit the purpose.

title: Evaluate claims and evidence
description: Assess the support for a claim by distinguishing facts, interpretations and assumptions, checking sources and considering reasonable alternatives.
oneStarDescription: Read a short argument and mark its main claim and at least one supporting reason.
twoStarDescription: Compare the claim with its source, identify an assumption and look for a plausible alternative explanation.
threeStarDescription: Summarise what the available evidence supports, what remains uncertain and what additional evidence would change your view.

title: Solve crosswords systematically
description: Use clue wording, crossings and theme clues to solve a crossword, keeping uncertain answers provisional until checked.
oneStarDescription: Solve straightforward clues and use crossing letters to test uncertain entries.
twoStarDescription: Recognise synonyms, abbreviations, wordplay or multiple meanings when simple definition clues are not enough.
threeStarDescription: Review theme relationships and crossing consistency, revising entries that conflict with the grid.

title: Combine words and visuals when learning
description: Pair a concise verbal explanation with a relevant diagram, timeline or sketch so that both express the same idea accurately.
oneStarDescription: Create a small labelled sketch or diagram beside a short written explanation.
twoStarDescription: Use a timeline, flow diagram or comparison table appropriate to the relationship being explained.
threeStarDescription: Explain the concept using the visual, then verify that no important relationship or qualification is missing.

title: Write effective emails
description: Write clear, appropriate email messages with a useful subject line, a concise body, a suitable tone and a clear next step.
oneStarDescription: Write a short email with a meaningful subject, greeting, clear request or message and appropriate closing.
twoStarDescription: Adjust formality and context for a familiar person versus an unfamiliar or professional recipient.
threeStarDescription: Write a follow-up that quotes only relevant context, answers questions clearly and avoids sharing sensitive information unnecessarily.

title: Connect new ideas to what you already know
description: Deepen understanding by asking why or how a claim works and linking it to relevant prior knowledge while distinguishing evidence from speculation.
oneStarDescription: For a concept, write one why-question and answer it in your own words using the material you studied.
twoStarDescription: Explain how a new idea relates to a familiar example or concept and where the comparison breaks down.
threeStarDescription: Give an explanation with a supporting example and name a condition where the example or analogy would mislead.

title: Explain how a visual communicates
description: Explain how an image and any text together make a point, instead of only describing what the picture shows.
oneStarDescription: For one visual document, say what it is mainly trying to communicate.
twoStarDescription: Identify visible choices, such as an image, the layout, or the words, and say what each one does.
threeStarDescription: Explain how those choices support or weaken the message, and mark one thing you cannot tell from the document alone.

title: Explain information clearly
description: Make information understandable to another person by identifying the main point, choosing relevant details and checking what the listener needs clarified.
oneStarDescription: Explain a familiar idea in a few sentences and ask the listener to say what they understood.
twoStarDescription: Explain the same idea to two audiences using different examples or levels of detail.
threeStarDescription: Answer follow-up questions, separate facts from assumptions and say what you do not know.

title: Everyday foreign-language conversation
description: Build practical conversational ability in another language, from prepared exchanges to maintaining a conversation and repairing misunderstandings.
oneStarDescription: Introduce yourself and complete a short prepared exchange on a familiar topic.
twoStarDescription: Hold a short conversation on a familiar subject, asking follow-up questions without relying entirely on a script.
threeStarDescription: Continue an unscripted conversation by paraphrasing, requesting clarification and explaining when a word is missing.

title: Georeference collection records
description: Match a locality description in a museum or specimen record to a plausible place on a map, retaining uncertainty when the location cannot be determined reliably.
oneStarDescription: Find a clearly stated locality on a map and record the chosen place according to the project’s instructions.
twoStarDescription: Compare names, historical spellings and nearby geographic clues when more than one place seems possible.
threeStarDescription: Record why a match is preferred and flag ambiguous or insufficient evidence instead of inventing precision.
